newsitem.title: USA: USDA to hold meeting on safe cooking of burgers.
newsitem.headline: USDA to hold meeting on safe cooking of burgers.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department will hold a meeting Wednesday to determine how often hamburger turns brown before reaching a safely-cooked temperature that kills dangerous E.coli bacteria.

The agency's Food Safety and Inspection Service said the meeting will ask scientists, food service workers and other experts to talk about the risk of hamburger appearing to be fully cooked when its internal temperature has not yet reached a safe level of 160 degrees Fahrenheit.
The meeting will begin at 0830 EDT on Wednesday at the Washington Plaza Hotel in Washington, D.C.

Earlier this week, the USDA said an Arkansas meat processing firm recalled more than 40,000 lbs of frozen hamburger patties linked to an outbreak of E.coli disease in Colorado. The bacteria, sometimes mixed into meat from fecal material from slaughtered animals, is destroyed when cooking temperatures exceed 160 degrees.
Some strains of the E.coli bacteria can cause diarrhea, kidney failure and death.
